## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)
*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*
The *Avijjānīvaraṇa Sutta* (*Itivuttaka* 14; PTS It 7) is a short discourse from the first division of the *Itivuttaka* [SuttaCentral]. In this sutta, the Buddha asserts that he perceives no single hindrance other than ignorance (*avijjānīvaraṇa*) by which beings are so obstructed that they wander and transmigrate through *saṁsāra* for an immense period of time [SuttaCentral; Webster 2005]. Paired closely with the subsequent *Taṇhāsaṁyojana Sutta* (Iti 15), it highlights ignorance and craving as the primary impediments to human liberation and spiritual progress [Webster 2005].
Curated parallels recorded on SuttaCentral include full parallels in the Pali *Saṁyutta Nikāya* (SN 45.141–148), the Chinese *Madhyama Āgama* (MĀ 141), the *Saṁyukta Āgama* (SĀ 1239 and SĀ² 66), and T 765.1, alongside resembling parallels in Sanskrit fragments (SF 100, SHT Sutta 43), the *Dīgha Nikāya* (DN 31), and the *Ekottarika Āgama* (EĀ 26.1–4) [SuttaCentral]. Internally, DharmaNexus finds substantial formulaic reuse across the *Itivuttaka*, sharing its highest textual overlap with the following discourse, *Taṇhāsaṁyojana Sutta* (Iti 15, matching §§0.1–2.4), as well as opening and closing sequences with Iti 18, Iti 19, and Iti 27 [DharmaNexus]. DharmaNexus also aligns segments of the text with the Chinese *Ekottarika Āgama* (T 125, fascicle 5) [DharmaNexus].
